A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReAttention work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. V2 Appendices A and B correspond to v3 Appendices B and E, allowing retained material to be distinguished from additions.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, needle-retrieval experiments, efficiency measurements, hyperparameter ablations, and cache visualizations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds comparator results and throughput measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 retain position-agnostic top-k selection, voting, neighboring-span extraction, global/local cache retention, and positional embedding after selection. Appendix A newly documents prefilling and decoding; its inconsistencies do not establish an actual algorithm redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions use LongBench, L-Eval, InfiniteBench, single/multiple-needle retrieval, RULER, and the same natural-text cache-analysis examples. New task-category breakdowns and efficiency measurements do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds InfLLM to LongBench comparisons for three LLaMA models in Table 1 and StreamingLLM to their InfiniteBench comparisons in Table 2. DynamicNTK remains in the stated protocol despite losing its separate table label. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds throughput evaluation with 1024 generated tokens and batch sizes selected to utilize available GPU memory across 32K–256K contexts. V3 also omits the native-8K LongBench/L-Eval configuration reported in v2. The retained benchmark truncation, NTK scaling factor, and ReAttention hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C extends efficiency analysis by examining whether memory savings support larger batches and higher throughput. Existing hyperparameter ablations, attention case studies, RULER failure analysis, and t-SNE analyses are retained, including the material moved from Appendix B to E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed protocols, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for the evaluated results.

E6.justification: V3 substantially expands reported results through task-category LongBench scores, added comparator scores, and throughput measurements, while matched existing scores remain unchanged. Table 2 newly shows StreamingLLM averaging 15.71 versus ReAttention's 15.36 for LLaMA3.2, qualifying its superiority caption. Table 7 reports 43.380 versus 40.595 tokens/s at 32K using batches 8 and 2, respectively, rather than demonstrating a same-batch speedup. V2's native-8K benchmark row is removed, and language-group summaries are replaced by task-category summaries.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 and the three motivating conditions remain unchanged. Neither the added pseudocode nor the expanded discussion introduces a new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of training-free unbounded context under sufficient memory, performance comparable to full attention, retrieval over millions of tokens, and efficient Triton implementation. Added evidence does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly distinguishes latency at identical batch sizes from throughput under memory-capacity constraints and interprets larger feasible batches as an efficiency benefit. Existing explanations of position-agnostic retrieval and limitations on synthetic, incoherent text remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds prefilling and decoding pseudocode, a project-code access pointer in the abstract, and batch-size/generation-length details for efficiency evaluation. This substantially expands implementation documentation. However, Algorithm 1 resets the cache inside the chunk loop, and both algorithms use global/local slices inconsistent with Section 2, limiting their reproducibility value.

R1.justification: New Appendix D substantially expands positioning within token eviction and cache compression, covering DCP, Scissorhands, SnapKV, DuoAttention, PyramidKV, PyramidInfer, Gemfilter, LongGen, VATP, and InfiniPot. It explicitly relates ReAttention's context extrapolation to these cache-selection approaches; these citations are not additional evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: V3 makes limited prose refinements, updates author affiliations and publication headers, adds acknowledgements, and reorganizes the appendices around pseudocode, effectiveness, efficiency, related work, and cache analysis. The main section sequence and most explanatory text remain intact.

P2.justification: Benchmark presentation is substantially reorganized: v2's six-panel overview disappears, v3 adds a main-text LongBench table, and the detailed benchmark table replaces language columns with task categories. InfiniteBench gains comparator rows, and two algorithm blocks plus TTFT/throughput tables are added. Other analytical figures are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Additional comparators, task-level results, throughput evidence, code-access information, and related-work discussion strengthen the paper's assessment and context. However, the new pseudocode contradicts the retained cache procedure, and Table 5 duplicates the LLaMA3.2-3B label on the block matching v2's 70B results. These newly introduced reproducibility and attribution problems make the net quality benefit uncertain.
